{"basis":"measured","fact_type":"defect","name":"ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): an agent's decision made under a person's delegation cannot be recorded as that. The approver edge holds one Contributor, and the rung that would link an agent to the person it acts for (ACTS_FOR, git's author/committer split) was designed on 2026-07-22 and deferred. So on flo2 the principal is recorded and the deciding agent is not, and a local store could record the agent only by naming it approver, which drops the principal","source":"art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29 (item I1; friction #2, #21)","statement":"RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-29, triaging art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29 under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed.

① OBSERVED. The flo2 design "ideal knowledge graph" (50f966697d6c5024) was worked by a DESIGNER agent through the claude.ai flo2 connector, reflow2 0.74.0. A separate OWNER agent (Contributor who:owner, kind automated_agent) decided under Anthony's written delegation. set_decision_status(approver: "who:owner") was refused: "An approval recorded through flo2 is always the signed-in person's own". The workaround was to leave approver out, so flo2 filled in who:acct-23984879ca (Anthony), then quote the owner's verdict in `chose` and draw authored_by role=reviewer → who:owner. That costs 2–3 extra calls per settled decision, about 30 over three rounds. The owner itself called it a failure of "who asserts" (test 2). Expected: the record says the owner agent decided, under Anthony's delegation. NOT affected: attribution of ordinary writes, which is recorded, as the signed-in account.

② PRECEDENT, searched in both designs.
· flo2: req:an-approval-in-a-shared-design-is-the-signed-in-persons, cap:the-gateway-binds-approvals-to-the-signed-in-person, and fact:root-cause-the-door-rebinds-approver-and-says-so-only-in-its-refusal-2026-09-28. So the refusal is DESIGNED behaviour.
· reflow2: dec:idea-may-a-caller-asserted-identity-be-trusted-and-for-what (open) and req:a-session-names-the-person-it-writes-for-and-the-server-remembers-it, which is attribution only and never approves.
· flo2: dec:idea-somebody-assigns-who-may-decide, option (d), "the owner may delegate a decision" (open).
Nothing recorded an agent deciding FOR a person.

③ CANDIDATES from the bones.
(a) GOVERNANCE: flo2 wrongly refuses a legitimate approver.
(b) INTENT/SCHEMA: reflow2 cannot represent an agent acting for a principal.
(c) NOT IN THE SUSPECTED COMPONENT: flo2 keeps no identity for the acting client at all, so even a willing reflow2 would receive nothing to record.
(d) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG: an approval showing Anthony's account is not false provenance, because the authority IS his.

④⑤ MEASURED 2026-09-29.
· (a) REFUTED. flo2's bindApprovals (services/edge-gateway/src/identity.ts), run in-process on the reported shapes with node --experimental-strip-types:
  - {status: accepted, approver: who:owner} → refused with the reported text;
  - no approver → filled with the caller's id.
  That is req:an-approval-in-a-shared-design-is-the-signed-in-persons working as written: an agent is not a signed-in person and must not be able to sign.
· (b) CONFIRMED.
  - schema/core.yaml, Contributor.kind reads: "An agent that acts on a person's behalf ACTS_FOR them (deferred rung)".
  - dec:design-authorship-identity (accepted, 2026-07-22) lists the later rungs "each needing the user on vocabulary": CLAIMS, ACTS_FOR (git's author/committer split), alternative authorship, and signing the content hash. CLAIMS was built; ACTS_FOR was not.
  - AUTHORED_BY carries roles {author, reviewer, approver} and dates only, with no on-behalf-of. The ACTS_FOR edge type does not exist in schema/*.yaml.
· (c) SUPPORTED. The gateway records the signed-in account on every write. The only clientInfo in its source is its own outgoing handshake (reflow2-client.ts, minter.ts). No code keeps which agent or client called.
· (d) PARTLY UPHELD. The approver edge naming Anthony is TRUE under his delegation. What is missing is the agent that exercised it and the delegation that authorised it, not a correct principal. So the report's "false provenance" is overturned to "INCOMPLETE provenance".

⑥ CLASS: a rung of the who-axis was designed, named as deferred in the schema's own text, and nothing re-asks it when its case arrives. Every write made through flo2 by an agent is this case: claude.ai, Grok and Claude Code all act for a signed-in person. So fixing ACTS_FOR would reach every hosted agent write, not only this exercise. Same shape as fact:the-tier-deferral-is-due-to-be-re-asked-2026-09-26: a deferral with no trigger.

⑦⑧ OWED. No pinning test and no fix yet; the vocabulary is Anthony's call (the rung "needs the user on vocabulary"). The companion idea is recorded as a brainstorm. A class-pinning test would assert that a settlement made by an agent under a delegation reads back naming the agent, the principal and the delegation.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED. Whether flo2 should pass the acting client's identity (MCP clientInfo, which a client self-declares) to reflow2: that is attribution on trust and has the same bounds as writes_for. Whether an agent with a standing delegation should be able to SETTLE at all, or only record the principal's settlement.
